title: Tszyu vs Fundora: Boxer's Dog Pablo Fights for Life | Brain Infection
text:
Tim tszyu Faces Personal Battle Alongside world Title Rematch with Fundora Australia’s boxing star Tim Tszyu is preparing for a crucial rematch with Sebastian fundora on July 20, but his training camp has been unexpectedly impacted by a deeply personal crisis: the severe illness of his beloved French bulldog, Pablo. The revelation underscores the emotional fortitude Tszyu must summon as he approaches a defining moment in his career.
Tszyu,30,departs for Las Vegas this Friday to finalize preparations for the WBC super welterweight championship fight against Fundora. However, in the lead-up to his departure, the fighter disclosed the harrowing ordeal his “best mate” of nearly a decade has been enduring – a brain infection requiring major surgery. This latest challenge comes after a previous setback two years ago, when a dog attack left Tszyu with 26 stitches before a fight with Carlos Ocampo .
“Dogs become your kids,” Tszyu shared,revealing the profound impact of Pablo’s condition. “They’re your best mate. So it was a hard time. Every day I’d go visit him in the ICU… it’s probably the hardest situation I’ve ever been in. Just the uncontrollable. Not knowing what is going to happen. The fact your dog is seizing, learning how to stand back up, learning how to walk – it was hard on the heart.”
Did you know? -Tszyu’s father, Kostya Tszyu, was also a world champion boxer. Kostya was inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2011, solidifying his legacy in the sport. Tim is aiming to follow in his father’s footsteps. The timing of Pablo’s illness coincided with the most intense phase of Tszyu’s sparring, forcing him to navigate a arduous emotional landscape while maintaining focus on his upcoming fight. He described the experience as a test of his mental resilience, a quality he believes he lacked during his first encounter with Fundora, which ended in a split decision.
“It was ‘how am I going to figure this out while staying focused?'” Tszyu explained in an interview with Main Event’s I’m Damon. “It was hard, juggling. Your mind is always with the pup. but I was able to push through. There were actually a couple of times I was getting smashed in the gym, just trying to push through, and in the back of my head I was thinking ‘if Pablo can go through what he has, what’s this little bit of pain right now?'”

Tszyu emphasized the importance of compartmentalization, a skill he acknowledges he previously lacked. “Because when I got cut [in the first Fundora fight], I wasn’t thinking about moving on, I was thinking about what’s happening now-the cut.” He believes his ability to remain present and focused,despite the emotional turmoil surrounding Pablo’s health,represents a significant improvement. “The fact I’ve had such a big distraction in front of me and I’ve been able to block it off and focus on what I have to do, that was a real test.”
Fortunately,Pablo is now on the road to recovery,though still experiencing some dizziness. “Pablo is OK,” Tszyu said with a smile. “He’s got a long road to recovery. Still gets a bit dizzy.But he’s in a good place and we’re in a good place. We’re looking after him. It’s given us a better viewpoint on life.”
The Tszyu family faces challenges on multiple fronts. Tim’s younger brother,Nikita,is also preparing for his return to the ring in August after a year-long recovery from a left hand injury. Nikita underwent surgery last October and has experienced setbacks in his rehabilitation. He recently confirmed he is back to punching at full strength, though cautiously.
“A couple of months,” Nikita Tszyu told Fox Sports Australia when asked when he resumed full-power punching. “Hard surfaces? Maybe a month. Going hard on the heavy bag for a month. Heads? One day.” He added that a recent sparring session, despite some lingering discomfort, proved encouraging.
Looking ahead, a potential December blockbuster fight against Michael zerafa looms for Tim Tszyu should he defeat Fundora. nikita, though, downplayed any involvement in family drama, stating, “I couldn’t care less what he’s said in the past – I say stupid s*** all the time. I say things I don’t mean all the time. And if he meant it, good on him, but I don’t care. I’m going to be respectful.”
Tim Tszyu, reflecting on past setbacks against Fundora and Bakhram Murtazaliev, views this year as a chance for redemption. “There’s no such thing as a successful story without failures,” he stated. “A couple of bumps on the road doesn’t mean you’re completely out. so this year is gonna be like a vengeance year. It started with Joey Spencer and it’s gonna keep on going.And when I rewrite this chapter, it’s gonna be one hell of a story.”
He expressed excitement about fighting at the MGM Grand for the first time, framing it as the realization of a childhood dream. “Look, everyone dreams of certain things as a young kid. Maybe you thought you were going to be an astronaut,or you say these [other] ridiculous things. I’m actually living it. I’m living what I said I would do as a kid – the things people would laugh at. But I’m here, living the superhero character. And it’s what life’s about for me. It should be for everyone.”
Fans can watch Tszyu vs Fundora 2 & pacquiao vs Barrios live on Sunday, July 20 at 10 AM AEST on Main Event on Kayo Sports.
The Mental Game: how Tim Tszyu Masters Resilience Tim Tszyu’s journey to the top of the boxing world is a testament to more than just physical prowess. As highlighted by the challenges surrounding his beloved dog Pablo and his brother Nikita’s recovery, Tszyu is actively building mental fortitude, a critical component for success both inside and outside the ring. Tszyu’s ability to compartmentalize,as mentioned earlier,is central to navigating these emotional hurdles.
The ability to focus, especially with external stressors, isn’t an inherent trait; it’s a skill honed over time through self-awareness and practice.Tszyu reveals this in his own journey.He readily admits to less than perfect mental control in the first Fundora fight. Now, he is displaying a new-found resilience.
The Impact of Mental Fortitude on Performance The link between mental strength and athletic performance is well-documented. according to sports psychologists, athletes who master high-pressure situations often display:
Enhanced Focus: The capacity to block out distractions and maintain concentration on the task at hand. Emotional Regulation: The ability to manage emotions in response to adversity. Self-Belief: A strong sense of confidence and belief in one’s abilities. Resilience: The ability to bounce back from setbacks and disappointments. These factors become especially important in combat sports, where split-second decisions can determine the outcome of a fight. Tszyu appears to be putting the tools to work,as his upcoming rematch against Fundora will determine his future in the sport [[3]] .
